newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BelgoLux 1995 current account surplus revised up.
newsitem.headline: BelgoLux 1995 current account surplus revised up.

text.p: The Belgian National Bank said on Friday it had revised up its estimation of the 1995 current account surplus of the Belgian-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) to 450 billion Belgian francs from 421 billion francs.
The BNB also said the surplus in the first eight months of 1996 rose to 311 billion francs from 294 billion in the same 1995 period.

Belgium and Luxembourg have been joined in a currency union since March 5, 1922, and normally published combined current account data. The surplus is a measure of the two countries' positive financial position to the rest of the world.
Under the European Union's Maastricht Treaty on economic and monetary union, Belgium and Luxembourg are obliged also to provide individual breakdowns of the current account data.
This was done for the first time in October 1996, covering the whole 1995 period, which showed that Belgium accounted for around three quarters of the surplus.
